headline: IRGC Navy says safe Hormuz transit will be ensured
dek: Trump wrote: 'Assuming Iran agrees to give what has been agreed to, which is, perhaps, a big assumption, the already legendary Epic Fury will be at an end, and the highly effective Blockade will allow the Hormuz Strait to be OPEN TO ALL, including Iran. If they don't agree, the bombing starts, and…
sources: Donald Trump, Truth Social post (Wednesday morning US) + IRGC Navy statement on X (Wednesday); reported by Al Jazeera
fault_line: Deal or double-down? Trump offers an open strait if Iran 'gives what has been agreed to' — but Tehran has not accepted, and refusal means bombing 'much higher' than before.

sections.what_happened: Trump wrote: 'Assuming Iran agrees to give what has been agreed to, which is, perhaps, a big assumption, the already legendary Epic Fury will be at an end, and the highly effective Blockade will allow the Hormuz Strait to be OPEN TO ALL, including Iran. If they don't agree, the bombing starts, and it will be, sadly, at a much higher level and intensity than it was before.' Same day, the IRGC Navy said safe transit through Hormuz will be ensured 'as the US threats end and with new procedures in place' (procedures unspecified), and Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman said Tehran was reviewing a US proposal and would convey its view via mediator Pakistan. Context: Axios-reported one-page, 14-point memorandum (Hormuz reopening, enrichment moratorium, sanctions relief, frozen-asset release) relayed by Reuters via Samakal; Iranian lawmaker Ebrahim Rezaei called the Axios text 'more of an American wish list than a reality'.
sections.what_verified: Trump post quoted verbatim by Al Jazeera (T2) and the Forbes mirror; Reuters (T1, via Samakal relay) confirms Iran reviewing a new US proposal via Pakistan and the Axios 14-point memo outline; IRGC statement via Al Jazeera.
sections.what_disputed: Counterpoint: Tehran's public line is unchanged — Rezaei (Nov 3) called the US response 'not convincing' and tied any reopening to all seven Iranian conditions; lawmaker Ebrahim Rezaei dismissed the Axios text as a US wish list; CNN/ICG analysis notes Trump faces a deal-or-double-down choice, not a settled deal. No signed agreement, no published text, no Iranian acceptance on record.
sections.why_matters: Trump's ultimatum in his own words: open strait or much heavier bombing — the deal that decides Hormuz. Claim-bust frame: no deal is signed; Tehran is still 'reviewing'.
